newsitem.title: INDIA: India rice exports seen rising on fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: India rice exports seen rising on fresh demand.

text.p: Indian rice exports are expected to pick up on a surge in demand from South Africa, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka after an increase in U.S. rice prices, traders said on Thursday.
"India's parboiled rice exports have a very good chance to pick up," Rashmi Bhimjayani, a leading Bombay foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.
Bhimjayani said Saudi Arabia, along with South Africa and neighbouring countries, had traditionally bought parboiled rice from the United States, but U.S. prices this year had risen.
"Due to that, Indian parboiled rice has captured a sizeable share of the Saudi Arabian market," Bhimjayani said.
He said Indian parboiled rice was currently quoted at around $300 per tonne FOB, compared to more than $500 per tonne for U.S. rice.
He said two vessels of around 12,000 tonnes of rice each destined for Sri Lanka and two vessels bound for Syria were being loaded at Indian ports.
Bhimjayani said three to four vessels were also being currently loaded for shipments to countries in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
"This year South Africa, Syria, CIS countries and Iran are the main buyers for Indian rice," Bhimjayani said.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was currently quoted at $300 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $290, 15 percent at $250 and 25 percent at $235, the same as last week.
"Iran has bought around 125,000 tonne of Indian rice in the last two weeks," Bhimjayani said.
He said Indian rice prices were not expected to fall further as demand was growing.
Bhimjayani said that with the Vietnamese crop coming to an end, buyers would look to India and Pakistan. But Pakistan did not have a sizeable export surplus, he said.
"Therefore the demand for Indian rice will be continuous. I don't think the market will decline," Bhimjayani said.
